title: Normal algebras remain normal under separable scalar extension
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $B$ be a commutative $k$-algebra, and let $K/k$ be a separable field extension [def-pc-field-extension, def-weil-pbc-separable-field-extension]: every finitely generated subextension is separably generated. Suppose $B$ is a normal ring [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], meaning that every prime localization of $B$ is an integrally closed domain. Then $B\otimes_k K$ is a normal ring: for every prime ideal $\mathfrak q$ of $B\otimes_k K$, the localization $(B\otimes_k K)_{\mathfrak q}$ is an integrally closed domain. Here the tensor product is the commutative tensor-product algebra [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], with $(b\otimes c)(b^{\prime}\otimes c^{\prime})=bb^{\prime}\otimes cc^{\prime}$ and unit $1\otimes1$. Neither algebraicity of $K/k$ nor finite generation of $B$ is required; the zero algebra and disconnected normal rings are included.
